Durham Forest  is probably one of the busiest spots in Ontario right now. The narrow trails or single track are one directional made to go in counter clockwise loops so mountain bikers can social distance adequately.  The double track loops are two directional and leave much better space for social distancing.  There is no washroom facilities at present.  Keep your eyes open for poison and ticks.

We did two of the major loops - White Pine and Spruce, and a few of the smaller ones: Knotty but Nice, Logs Over Easy, parts of Ogre and Out, and Lickety Split for a total of 9.4km in about 2 hours. All paths well maintained but seem to be primarily for bikers (and there were LOTS of them...). Smaller trails are marked as one way only. As a hike the various loops felt disjointed, but the main trail is pretty flat and has low variety. I would say the only thing that makes it moderate is the length, otherwise it is easy. Lots of bugs and poison ivy.

Durham Region Forest opened officially, Friday May 29th, 2020 post Covid-19 lockdown.  Please note double track trails are bi-directional, but all single tracks are one-way only trails.   These one-way, single track trails now have signage at the beginning and end of each trail, to help keep all people moving generally in a counter clockwise motion around Durham Region Forest.
